rows.jp: 教室に顔を出すと、冬子がいた。
rows.en: When I stopped by the classroom, Touko was there.

ghs.en: When I showed face in the classroom, Touko was there.
ghs.assessment: 教室に顔を出す means to drop by or look into the classroom. 'Showed face' is a literal calque rather than idiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'When I dropped by the classroom, Tōko was there.'

highlights.text: When I showed face in the classroom, Touko was there.

ghs.en: I was surprised, and stood still.
Taichi: "...Kirihara."

rows.jp: 気怠げに視線が、まるで俺の背後でも見通すかのように、虚ろに泳いだ。
rows.en: Her listless gaze wandered vacantly, as if it could see straight through me and beyond.

ghs.en: Her languid gaze was swimming vacantly, as if it were looking straight through to behind me.

rows.jp: 冬子の頬がこけていた。

ghs.en: Touko's cheeks were sunken.

rows.en: Her skin had lost its color.

ghs.en: Her complexion looked bad too.
Hair frayed as well.
ghs.assessment: Frayed hair is a permissible poetic image. The remaining problem is collocation and polish.

rows.jp: 命のともしびは、確実に小さくなっていた。
rows.en: The flame of her life was unmistakably dwindling.

ghs.en: The light of her life had become truly faint.

rows.jp: 関心ない様子で机に顔を伏せる。
rows.en: Apparently uninterested, she lowered her face to the desk.

ghs.en:
She lays her face on the desk, looking
disinterested.
ghs.assessment: 机に顔を伏せる means to lower or bury one's face against the desk. 'Lays her face on the desk' is not idiomatic for that posture.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She lowers her face to the desk, apparently indifferent.'

highlights.text:
She lays her face on the desk, looking
disinterested.

rows.jp: 冬子は誰にも触れないまま、朽ちていくのだろうか。
rows.en: Would Touko simply waste away without ever touching another person?

ghs.en:
Seems Touko has stayed like this, not touching
nor touched by anybody, rotting away.
ghs.assessment: Reciprocal loneliness is latent in context, though GHS expands what the unit states explicitly.
ghs.remedy: Keep the loneliness without unnecessary explanatory expansion.

highlights.text:
Seems Touko has stayed like this, not touching
nor touched by anybody, rotting away.

rows.jp: 人類の終わったこの世界で。
rows.en: Here, in this world after the end of humanity.

ghs.en: of this world where mankind had ended.

rows.jp: 彼女はショックに耐えられなかったのか。
rows.en: Had the shock been more than she could bear?

ghs.en: She could perhaps not endure the shock,

rows.jp: 誰だって最後は一人で死ぬ。
rows.en: Everyone dies alone in the end.

ghs.en: Everybody, at the end, is alone in death.

rows.jp: けど死ぬまでは、生きていないといけないのに。
rows.en: But until you die, you have to keep living.

ghs.en:
But until death, it is out of the question
to not be living.

rows.jp: 俺は近寄って、声をかけた。
rows.en: I went over and spoke to her.

ghs.en: I approached and called out to her,
as gently as I could.

rows.jp: それが偽善であったとしても……構わない。
rows.en: Even if it was hypocrisy... I didn’t care.

ghs.en: Though this may have been hypocritical... it didn't matter.

rows.jp: 俺は偽善を行うために、在るのだから。
rows.en: After all, I exist to practice hypocrisy.

ghs.en: Because I exist for the purpose of carrying out hypocrisy.

rows.jp: 「気にくわないこともあるだろうけど、明日から部活、来てみないか？」
rows.en: “I know there’s still plenty you don’t like, but... why not start coming to the club tomorrow?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I know you can't really stomach it, but couldn't you try coming to Club starting tomorrow?"
Touko: "...eh?"

rows.jp: 困惑と戸惑いを貼りつけて、彼女は伏していた顔をあげた。
rows.en: Touko looked up from the desk, confusion and uncertainty still fixed on her face.

ghs.en: Gluing puzzlement to bewilderment, she brought up her prostrate head.
ghs.assessment: The source figuratively says she raises her lowered face wearing confusion and bewilderment. 'Gluing puzzlement to bewilderment' incorrectly makes one emotion adhere to another.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Wearing an expression of confusion, she raises her lowered face.'

highlights.text: Gluing puzzlement to bewilderment, she brought up her prostrate head.

rows.jp: 憔悴したその面差しが、緋色に色づけされてどこか悲壮な印象を与えた。
rows.en: Her haggard face had gone scarlet, giving her a strangely tragic air.

ghs.en: Her emaciated features turned a bright scarlet, and left me with an impression in some respects tragic.
Taichi: "No?"
ghs.assessment: The practical intent survives; only pragmatic register is off.
ghs.remedy: Use a natural line with the same conversational force.

rows.jp: 机に水筒とサンドイッチの包みを置いた。
rows.en: I set a thermos and a package of sandwiches on her desk.

ghs.en: I put a bundle of sandwiches and the canteen on her desk,

rows.en: They were left over from the trip to the beach.

ghs.en: the leftovers of the beach outing.

rows.jp: 一人分くらいはあった。
rows.en: There was enough for one person.

ghs.en: There's about enough for one person.

rows.jp: 冬子がそれをじっと凝視する。

ghs.en: Touko stares at them intently.

rows.jp: 「ゆっくり食べないと、胃が受けつけないからな」
rows.en: “Eat slowly. Your stomach won’t take it otherwise.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You gotta eat slowly, the stomach won't accept it otherwise."
Touko: "...have no... appetite."
A husked voice.
ghs.assessment: 掠れた声 is a hoarse or rasping voice. 'Husked voice' uses the wrong participle.

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yeah I get it, so eat."

rows.jp: ゆっくりと手が伸びる。

ghs.en: Slowly she reaches with her hands,
ghs.assessment: The Japanese subject is one hand. 'Her hands' changes the number and leaves the clause hanging into the next line.

highlights.text: Slowly she reaches with her hands,

ghs.en: unwraps the package,
and gives tiny gnaws.
ghs.assessment: 小さく囓る means to take a small nibble. 'Gives tiny gnaws' is not idiomatic English and pluralizes the single action.

ghs.en: Taichi: "...slowly now. There's also water if you need."
Touko: "......ngh."
She covers her mouth.
Taichi: "Ah, you alright?"
Touko: "I'm alright, it's all good."
Shaken off.

rows.jp: 挙措は弱々しかったが、拒絶の意志は確かだった。
rows.en: Her movement was feeble, but the rejection behind it was unmistakable.

ghs.en: Her behavior is feeble, but there is also an intent of rejection, definitely.
ghs.assessment: The source contrasts her weak movements with a definite will to reject him. The English's 'there is also ... definitely' is ungrammatical and weakens that contrast.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Her movements were feeble, but her rejection was unmistakable.'

highlights.text: Her behavior is feeble, but there is also an intent of rejection, definitely.

ghs.en: Taichi: "...Kiriharaaa."
The mood is awkward.
Touko: "I'll... take this yes."
ghs.assessment: The source simply says 'I'll take this.' The appended 'yes' has no source basis and produces unnatural syntax.

ghs.en: Taichi: "Eh?"
Touko: "So I'll eat it home."
ghs.assessment: English requires 'eat it at home,' not 'eat it home.'

ghs.en: Taichi: "Will you... you sure?"
ghs.assessment: The proposition survives, with only punctuation and an added shade of certainty.
ghs.remedy: Restore the source degree of certainty and punctuation.

ghs.en: Touko: "...yeah."
Touko: "Thank you."

rows.jp: すんなりと礼の言葉を口にする。

ghs.en: Words of politeness flow smoothly from her mouth.

rows.jp: 「俺さ……日曜、部活に出ようと思うんだけど」
rows.en: “I’m thinking of going to the club on Sunday.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You know, me... I'm thinking of going to club on Sunday."
Taichi: "If you want to, you can come too."
Taichi: "We'll send out an SOS."

rows.jp: 「たいして広範囲には届かないみたいだけど」

ghs.en: Taichi: "It doesn't look like the reach will be that extensive, though."

rows.jp: 「指向性と帯域の調整はいくらでもできるから」
rows.en: “But we can adjust the directionality and bandwidth however we like.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There's so many possible bandwidth and direction settings we could use after all."

rows.en: “That’s what the new club is about.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Those will be new club activities, then."
ghs.assessment: それ refers to the SOS-broadcasting activity as the new club activity. 'Those' incorrectly points back to multiple settings and changes the number.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That will be the new club activity.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Those will be new club activities, then."

ghs.en: Taichi: "...not bad innit?"
Touko: "...I'd say."
ghs.assessment: The answer is intelligible, but loses the connective so and the source ellipsis.

rows.jp: 少しだけ、冬子との悪関係を修復できた気がした。
rows.en: It felt as though I had managed to ease the bad blood between us, just a little.

ghs.en: It felt that my bad relationship with Touko had mended, just a tiny bit.
